questions.q: Which junction is point A of the gastrinoma triangle?
opts: Junction of second and third duodenal portions
Junction of pancreatic body and neck
Junction of cystic duct and common bile duct
Junction of common bile duct and pancreatic tail
questions.exp: Point A is the junction of the cystic duct and CBD. (Book p60)

questions.q: Point B of the gastrinoma triangle is the junction of the:
opts: Second and third portions of the duodenum
Cystic duct and common bile duct
First and second portions of the duodenum
questions.exp: Point B is the junction of the second and third portions of the duodenum. (Book p60)

questions.q: The pancreatic landmark at point C is the junction of the:
opts: Body and neck of the pancreas
questions.exp: Point C is the junction of the body and neck of pancreas. (Book p60)

questions.q: Which group contains all three boundaries identified for the gastrinoma triangle?
opts: CBD/ampulla; D1–D2 junction; pancreatic body–tail junction
Cystic-duct/CBD junction; D2–D3 junction; pancreatic body–neck junction
Pylorus; ligament of Treitz; pancreatic tail

units.title: Types and Comparisons
units.guide:
Sporadic (80%) versus MEN1-associated (20%) differ in number/size, age, sex, location and risk.
Sporadic tumours are listed as more aggressive; MEN1 disease is usually smaller and less aggressive.
Keep the note separating insulinoma as the commonest functional pancreatic NET overall.

units.title: Triangle and Gastrin Effects
units.guide:
Triangle points: cystic duct/CBD, D2–D3 and pancreatic body–neck junctions.
Gastrin → parietal cells → HCl; mucosal injury yields GU/DU.
Acid can inactivate pancreatic enzymes, linking to diarrhoea, steatorrhoea and malabsorption.

units.title: Clinical Features
units.guide:
Abdominal pain is the most important symptom; PUD is the commonest manifestation.
Unusual D2+ ulcers, refractory GU/DU, recurrence and diarrhoea raise suspicion in the page.
Diarrhoea has secretory and enzyme-inactivation/steatorrhoea components.

units.title: Tests and Imaging
units.guide:
Fasting gastrin: <200 normal, 200–1000 needs confirmation; preserve the source's >1000 wording.
Secretin gives a paradoxical gastrin rise ≥200 pg/mL in the printed test.
SRS/¹¹¹In, octreotide rationale, EUS caveat, BAO/MAO and DOTATATE note are inventoried.

units.title: Treatment and Surgical Anatomy
units.guide:
MEN1: high-dose PPI 60–80 mg; surgery when >2.5 cm.
Sporadic: PPI + octreotide then surgery; procedure follows head/body-tail/duodenal location.
The page says gastrectomy is not required and names liver as the commonest metastasis site.
